# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Datasec/NexusAI RD-148 round 2 @ `ea4d229`, TIER 1) | **GO-with-findings — and it built a STRONGER contrast than the builder, then found the CLASS the round had only fixed an instance of.** Re-ran the builder's A/B/C and added **B2**: round-1 product code byte-identical, round-1 cells, and **ONLY the fixture line changed** (`1 file changed, 1 insertion, 4 deletions`) — the three revoke cells flip red while the seven render/date cells that never touch the status node stay GREEN. **That built-in negative control is what rules out 'the edit just broke everything', and B1 could not: B1 moves 140 lines, so it leaves 'the fixture did it' an inference.** Every finding proved byte-identical between base and head per-function, so none is charged to this round. **N-1 (Major): the defect class F-1 belongs to is still live in `load()` in the same file** — a failed provisioning load is silent, misrepresents the tenant's state, and a subsequent unguarded Save switches SCIM provisioning off. **N-4: the round's own new STRUCTURE cell does not guard the risk it appears to guard** — a check that cannot fail, inside the suite built to stop exactly that. | **1.0** | **🔴 Its verdict MAIL ARRIVED WITH A ZERO-BYTE BODY** — subject carried the verdict, findings did not travel. Measured with the `preview` discriminator and a same-read control (null on it, 200 chars on all four neighbours in one listing). **Nothing lost only because the brief specified a report path on disk.** `send_brief.sh`'s 40-char body refusal does not cover the QA agent's own mail path — the gap is in the path. Mail also mis-tagged `[Datasec/NexusAI ->]` instead of `[QA ->]`; routing is by subject. **It DID stop its servers and prove both ports 000** — the line the round-4 brief lacked, added to this one, and it worked. |
| QA agent (fleet, Datasec/NexusAI RD-361 round 4 @ `400718f`, TIER 1) | **GO-with-findings, BLOCKER CLOSED — and it widened the builder's own load-bearing census rather than checking it.** 24 real-server runs (12 states x 2 heads), each boot -> act at the wire -> interrupt -> boot on the SAME DATA_DIR, every 503 attributed to the server's own `[auth] DENY:` line. The census re-run over a WIDER frame than claimed — 678 tracked files PLUS all of `node_modules` (0 hits) PLUS the Docker build context (proving no shipped test helper can write the key) — with both writers driven at the wire and their stamps ASSERTED, all four computed-key `setSetting` sites checked and all three wholesale settings writers read individually. **It caught its OWN first probe design using an ungated route as the SUBJECT, so it could not fail**, and swapped to `/api/data-sources`. Two runs discarded and re-done because `restoreFromBackupsIfNeeded()` silently merged a tamper back — reported, not smoothed. Controls that flip BOTH ways (state I r3 503 -> r4 200; state C3 r3 200 -> r4 503). F-1 found a sentence MEASURED FALSE in two artefacts, and was scrupulous about what it would NOT charge to this round (PREVGEN pre-existing, both heads serve). F-2 named round 3's failure class one level down: a census correct when written and undefended by any test. | **1.0** | ~21 min. Frame limits named unprompted (`8eb94ce` a bulk import, so the age claim holds over recorded history only; it did not read Jira and said so). **That last gap was real: Wednesday's completion check found F-1's false sentence in a THIRD artefact, RD-361 comment 37266.** One housekeeping omission: it booted 24 servers and its housekeeping section never claims to have stopped them — `pane_close.sh` caught a listene

# Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."

> ## ℹ️ PATTERN FYI 2026-08-20 (extends the #723/#724 item below): s50 found P3 was
> already ON DEMO (#666 merged 08-12, shipped with the 08-14 discharge) while KS-584's
> "never against demo mid-development" hold read otherwise. Third instance of team
> holds being read differently by different hands — one shared rule at the CI cost
> conversation would close the class.
